target.title: feat(dashboard): add unlisted OpenClaw Bay demo
target.body:
## Summary

- add an unlisted, read-only OpenClaw Bay demo at `/bay-demo`
- turn the existing ClawSweeper status snapshot into an animated beach with live stage lanes, terminal pools, retrigger tunnels, repository filters, search, detail drawer, master-sweeper modes, and a bounded 20-outcome tide
- keep `/bay` unpublished and leave the existing Overview, issue triage, and PR proof triage navigation unchanged

![OpenClaw Bay browser proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brokemac79/clawsweeper/85c32598e6f2f929fe4b7648c49800d7ccdfaee0/docs/openclaw-bay-demo.jpg)

## Problem

The operational Overview is intentionally dense and table-oriented. Maintainers asked to try a more visual, playful way to see whether ClawSweeper is active without replacing the existing operational surfaces. This PR publishes the selected prototype as an explicitly experimental demo on the existing dashboard Worker.

## Implementation

- renders active work in Arriving, Setting up, Reviewing, Repairing, and Applying lanes using the existing worker snapshot
- raises a READY flag and lets the master sweeper animate proved forward movement
- treats any new `run_id` for the same GitHub item as a retrigger, using the tunnel/re-emergence path even when a poll first sees the new run in the same or a later lane
- shows Completed, Failed, and Cancelled only from explicit terminal evidence; disappearing workers stay CHECKING during the bounded confirmation grace period
- stores only a bounded terminal view: fewer than 20 current outcomes, the latest 20 washed outcomes retained for the 60-second wash animation, and at most 256 seen event IDs under the existing seven-day status TTL
- adds `Where's my crustacean?`, repository filters, GitHub/workflow detail links, patrol/on-change modes, local-only tide preview, reduced-motion handling, and hardened noindex/no-store/frame-blocked headers

## GitHub API And Runtime Load

Bay is a presentation over the existing cache-backed `/api/status` snapshot. It adds **no browser-to-GitHub requests and no new GitHub REST or GraphQL query path**. Terminal outcomes and timing samples are derived from workflow-job and recent-close data already collected for Overview.

Bay polls the Worker every 20 seconds versus Overview every 15 seconds: three rather than four status requests per minute after initial load, or 25% fewer browser-to-Worker requests. This is deliberately **not** described as 25% fewer upstream GitHub API calls: cache expiry, edge location, and concurrent viewers determine whether either status request causes a refresh. The defensible GitHub API claim is neutral/no-new-query-path, while browser polling load is lower.

## Validation

- `node --test test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` — 79/79 passed
- `pnpm run build:dashboard` — passed
- `pnpm run lint:dashboard` — passed
- `pnpm run lint:scripts` — passed
- `pnpm run dashboard:smoke -- http://127.0.0.1:8793` — passed; verified `/bay-demo`, `/bay` remains 404, security headers, shared status schema, zero direct GitHub requests, and all three WebP assets
- `pnpm run check` — passed on the rebased commit in Crabbox local-container `cbx_42c092e28737` (`violet-shrimp`, Playwright Noble image); the disposable Linux copy was normalised to LF and supplied `jq` before running the repository's complete check
- an earlier exact-commit run hit one transient failure in an unchanged wall-clock runtime-budget test; the complete check passed on rerun, while the failing test, apply runtime, package scripts, and Bay-focused proof were unchanged or green
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed

## Browser Proof

Tested locally at 1900x945 against the public cache-backed status snapshot:

- live crustaceans rendered across active and terminal lanes
- search located and highlighted GitHub item `#64319`
- repository filtering retained only the selected repository
- item selection opened the details drawer with safe GitHub/workflow links
- a live same-item retrigger used the tunnel path rather than READY/forward progress
- tide preview remained browser-only and did not change live outcome data
- no browser console errors or warnings

## Review Closeout

- `codex review --uncommitted` — clean after actioning retrigger classification, evidence-safe chat copy, and authoritative live-Bay fallback findings
- `codex review --base origin/main` — fresh post-rebase review clean; earlier findings were actioned for neutral completed-job terminal mapping and deferring terminal-event deduplication until the active feed settles, and the final review found no actionable defects
- independent public-boundary audit — clean: route remains public-but-unlisted, read-only, noindexed, frame-blocked, escaped, and free of direct GitHub/mutation paths

## Risks And Rollout

- `/bay-demo` is unlisted, not private. Anyone who knows or guesses the URL can open it; a maintainer-only rollout would need Cloudflare Access or separate application authentication.
- this is an experimental view, not a replacement for operational triage pages
- inline page CSS/JS is allowed by the current route-specific CSP; external files or CSP nonces would be a later hardening improvement if the demo becomes permanent
- the terminal feed is intentionally bounded and evidence-based, so it is not a historical ledger

## Release Note

Experimental: add an unlisted OpenClaw Bay dashboard demo that visualises the existing ClawSweeper worker state as an animated shoreline.

target.title: fix: isolate maintainer report publishing
target.body:
## Summary

- run Codex report generation with read-only repository tokens
- publish the bounded report artifact on a fresh runner with the write token
- deploy on a third runner so Cloudflare credentials never share a process tree with Codex

## Validation

- `pnpm run check`
- `actionlint .github/workflows/maintainer-activity-report.yml`
- Autoreview: no findings

## Exact-head live proof

Head: `27bd5fb9a7783be7b22db13761be9d42f32aef38`

- [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29156420597): Linux `pnpm check` and the Windows launcher passed.
- [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29156420618): Actions and JavaScript/TypeScript analysis passed.
- [First generation/publication run](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29156428766): generation used read-only repository tokens; a separate fresh runner minted the repository write token, published the generated artifact once, and revoked the token during cleanup; deployment was skipped.
- [Second generation/publication run](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29157839325): the same credential boundaries passed again and deployment was skipped. The live source data had changed, so this run produced a distinct report artifact and one corresponding publication rather than duplicating the first artifact.
- Focused integration coverage runs an identical artifact through publication twice and proves exactly one remote commit: the first attempt publishes and the second is a no-op. Empty artifacts, staging control files, additions, modifications, and deletions are covered.
- [Exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29156436804) accepted all prior code findings as resolved; its remaining request was completed live behavior proof.

Cloudflare deployment was explicitly disabled and was not exercised. Landing therefore still requires either an item-specific waiver for Cloudflare live proof or later authorization for that proof.
